summary: Checked 47 verifiable claims in tech-spec.md against actual codebase. Found 1 critical, 3 major, 4 minor issues. Critical: MeterRegistry will NOT be autoconfigured without spring-boot-starter-actuator — micrometer-core alone is insufficient. Major: BotConnectIT does not exist (referenced 2x); BotControllerIT:399 cited for token-leak assertions is wrong line (assertions live around :278-286); @Indexed.expireAfterSeconds is deprecated since Spring Data MongoDB 4.4. Minor issues: patterns.md line citations slightly off in two places.

findings.claim: tech-spec says (Decision 10 + Shared resources + Dependencies sections): adding only `io.micrometer:micrometer-core` to backend/build.gradle is sufficient for Spring Boot to autoconfigure the `MeterRegistry` bean ("`MeterRegistry` bean autoconfigured by Spring Boot when this jar is on classpath, even without `spring-boot-starter-actuator`"). The four webhook counters and Timer in Decision 10 inject this bean.
findings.reality: All Spring Boot autoconfig classes that produce a `MeterRegistry` bean (`MetricsAutoConfiguration`, `CompositeMeterRegistryAutoConfiguration`, `SimpleMetricsExportAutoConfiguration`, `JvmMetricsAutoConfiguration`) live under the package `org.springframework.boot.actuate.autoconfigure.metrics.*` — that package ships with the `spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure` JAR, which is pulled in only by `spring-boot-starter-actuator`. With ONLY `micrometer-core` on the classpath there is no `MeterRegistry` `@Bean` definition, no `SimpleMeterRegistry` is created, and `@Autowired MeterRegistry meterRegistry` in the controller/worker will fail context startup with `NoSuchBeanDefinitionException`. Verified via Spring Boot 3.5 docs (Context7).
findings.source: tech-spec.md Decision 10 (lines 135-138), Shared resources table (line 85), Dependencies section (line 298), Task 1 verify-smoke (line 402)
findings.fix: Either (a) switch the dependency to `spring-boot-starter-actuator` and explicitly disable the actuator endpoints in security/properties (e.g. `management.endpoints.web.exposure.exclude=*` + a SecurityConfig rule), OR (b) declare a `@Bean SimpleMeterRegistry meterRegistry() { return new SimpleMeterRegistry(); }` in a `@Configuration` class so the bean exists. Without one of these the AC16 counter assertions will never compile/run.

findings.claim: tech-spec references `BotConnectIT` as an existing test: (1) Acceptance Criteria line 387 — "No regressions in existing tests: `BotControllerIT`, `BotConnectIT`, `TelegramSenderIT`, `ProjectControllerIT`, `SecurityBlockTest` all stay green"; (2) Task 2 verify-smoke line 410 — `./gradlew test --tests *Sha256HexTest --tests *WebhookSecretVerifierTest --tests *BotConnectIT all green`.
findings.reality: There is no `BotConnectIT.java` anywhere under `backend/src/test/java/`. The connect-flow integration tests live INSIDE `backend/src/test/java/com/botfunnel/bot/BotControllerIT.java` (the file contains `postConnect_*` and `parallelSameToken*` tests). The other referenced files exist: `BotControllerIT.java`, `TelegramSenderIT.java`, `ProjectControllerIT.java`, `SecurityBlockTest.java`.
findings.fix: Replace `BotConnectIT` references with `BotControllerIT` (or with the specific connect tests, e.g. `--tests *BotControllerIT.postConnect_*`). The Task 2 smoke command will silently match zero tests today and pass without exercising the Connect regression.

findings.claim: tech-spec line 329 / line 478 — "AC18 — token-scrubber per log site via `ListAppender<ILoggingEvent>` filtered by `Logger.getName()` and `Level` — split per call site, no combined assertion (matches `BotControllerIT.java:399` precedent)."
findings.reality: `BotControllerIT.java:399` is not the token-leak assertion site. Line 399 is `.expectStatus().isEqualTo(502)` inside `postConnect_setWebhookTransientFailures_returns502WithCodeTelegramUnavailable`. The actual token-leak invariant lives around lines 278-286 (assertions using `TOKEN_REGEX.matcher(body).matches()` and `TOKEN_SUBSTRING.matcher(body).find()`).
findings.source: tech-spec.md line 329 (Testing Strategy AC18), Task 10 Files to read (line 478)
findings.fix: Update the line citation to `BotControllerIT.java:~278-286` (the assertNoTokenInBody helper-style block) or remove the specific line number and just cite `BotControllerIT` as the per-site `ListAppender` precedent.

findings.claim: tech-spec line 209 — `@Indexed(name="ttl_createdAt", expireAfterSeconds=7776000, partialFilter="...")` on `RawUpdate.createdAt`. Decision 8 + Data Models use the `expireAfterSeconds` attribute.
findings.reality: In Spring Data MongoDB 4.5.4 (the version on classpath via Spring Boot 3.5.0), `@Indexed.expireAfterSeconds` is marked `@Deprecated(since="4.4", forRemoval = true)` in `Indexed.java`. The current attribute is `expireAfter()` returning a duration String like `"90d"`. Using `expireAfterSeconds` will compile (and work at runtime) but generate a deprecation warning and is on the removal path.
findings.source: tech-spec.md line 209 (Data Models — RawUpdate field), Decision 8 (line 126)
findings.fix: Switch to the non-deprecated form: `@Indexed(name="ttl_createdAt", expireAfter="P90D", partialFilter="...")` or `expireAfter="90d"`. The 7776000 seconds = 90 days literal stays semantically identical.

findings.claim: tech-spec Solution paragraph (line 14) — "Worker (JobRunr-thread, blocking-safe per `patterns.md` line 59)". Also Decision 11 line 143 — "Worker uses `.block()` on inner reactive helpers — accepted per `patterns.md` line 59 (JobRunr thread ≠ Netty event-loop)".
findings.reality: patterns.md line 59 says: "**JobRunr recurring jobs.** Cleanup/maintenance jobs are registered as recurring jobs with explicit cron (e.g. `HardDeleteJob` daily at 03:00). Use `BackgroundJob`/`@Recurring` + idempotent semantics; jobs run on every replica but JobRunr's distributed lock prevents double-execution." Line 59 does not say anything about "blocking-safe on JobRunr thread" or "JobRunr thread ≠ Netty event-loop". The blocking-safe pattern is implicit (see `HardDeleteJob.java` using `.block()`) but is not documented on patterns.md line 59.
findings.fix: Either (a) drop the specific line citation and reference patterns.md "JobRunr recurring jobs" rule + the `HardDeleteJob`/`ProjectHardDeleteJob` precedents directly, or (b) add an explicit "JobRunr worker threads are safe to .block() (not Netty event-loop)" line to patterns.md and pin to the new line number.

findings.claim: tech-spec Risks R1 line 364 — "fall-back is Caffeine cache for Bot lookup (deferred per `patterns.md` line 119, only when measured)".
findings.reality: patterns.md line 119 is about per-call decrypt of bot tokens, not about Bot lookup caching: "Per-call decrypt; `requireValidTokenShape` runs BEFORE URI construction... Cache (Caffeine with short TTL) was rejected as premature — revisit when Epic 07 broadcast load profiles show measurable cost." The Caffeine-cache deferral principle is documented for the token-decrypt path, not for Bot-lookup. The principle is analogous but the citation is not exact.
findings.fix: Soften citation to "premature-caching deferral convention used elsewhere (e.g. patterns.md line 119 for token-decrypt cache)" or drop the line number and keep the spirit of the rule.

findings.claim: tech-spec Decision 11 line 143 — "static `BackgroundJob.enqueue` matches existing `@Recurring` precedent in `HardDeleteJob` / `ProjectHardDeleteJob` (no `JobScheduler` injection in codebase yet)."
findings.reality: HardDeleteJob.java and ProjectHardDeleteJob.java both use `@Recurring` (cron-scheduled) and do NOT call `BackgroundJob.enqueue(...)` at all. Their executor is JobRunr's recurring-job scheduler, not a static `BackgroundJob.enqueue` call. So the claim that "static `BackgroundJob.enqueue` matches existing `@Recurring` precedent" is misleading — `@Recurring` is a registration annotation, not an enqueue call. The codebase has NO existing `BackgroundJob.enqueue(...)` precedent (this is acknowledged in code-research.md line 127: "No existing one-shot `BackgroundJob.enqueue(...)` call exists in the codebase").
findings.fix: Rephrase: "static `BackgroundJob.<X>enqueue(lambda)` is the official JobRunr API (verified via Context7) and avoids introducing a new injected bean type. The codebase has no prior `BackgroundJob.enqueue` call (only `@Recurring` registrations), so this introduces a new pattern — flagged in Risks."

findings.claim: tech-spec Task 10 line 478 — files-to-read includes `backend/src/test/java/com/botfunnel/bot/BotControllerIT.java` "(race-test + token-leak assertion precedents)". The exact race-test cited elsewhere (line 478 R3-related) and tech-spec testing strategy line 325 reference `Flux.range(0, 2).parallel(2)` shape.
findings.reality: BotControllerIT.java does have the race-test precedent at lines 511-580 (postConnect_parallelSameToken_exactlyOneSucceeds_otherReturns409 and postConnect_parallelSameProjectDifferentTokens_*), but they use `Mono.zip(r1, r2, ...)` rather than `Flux.range(0, 2).parallel(2).flatMap(...)`. The test pattern is correct but the syntactic shape differs from what the tech-spec testing strategy describes for AC5 (line 325).
findings.source: tech-spec.md line 325 (Testing Strategy AC5), line 478 (Task 10 files to read)
findings.fix: Adopt the existing `Mono.zip(...)` shape in 04b race tests for consistency with the codebase precedent, OR explicitly note in the tech-spec that 04b uses `Flux.parallel` because the AC5 race involves a status pair `{200, 200}` (not `{200, 409}`) which is shape-independent.
